idiom_name: Slick column[Int]("id", O.PrimaryKey, O.AutoInc) (+ Doobie returning)
implementation_notes: With Slick the identity field is declared in the table class - def id = column[Int]("id", O.PrimaryKey, O.AutoInc) - and the mapped case class keeps it optional (Option[Int]) because a new row has no key yet; AutoInc also tells Slick which column the database returns after an insert, so the key comes back with users returning users.map(_.id). Doobie/skunk-style code instead uses a RETURNING clause on the insert statement, and java.util.UUID is a supported Slick column type for application-generated keys. The classic key-generator object is replaced by the column option plus the returning projection; a sequence pre-fetch is the strategy when keys must be known before the insert.
pitfalls: AutoInc must be marked on the key column: many databases silently ignore non-AutoInc columns in the returned row, so the key read-back fails with no obvious error when the option is missing.
Option[Int] in the row type pushes the unsaved state into every conversion between model and row; mapping a placeholder 0 instead loses the distinction between 'new' and row 0.
Composite keys are declared with primaryKey(...) rather than O.PrimaryKey and then appear in every query and join, so prefer a surrogate key unless the table really is a link table.
